hints: Focus on what each observation tells you separately, fizzing with acid points to one anion and blue litmus points to one cation.
Fizzing with dilute HCl means $\text{CO}_2$ is released, so R must contain carbonate or hydrogencarbonate, while gas turning red litmus blue is ammonia, so R must contain $\text{NH}_4^+$.
Now check charge balance, $\text{NH}_4^+$ is +1 and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ is -2, so work out how many ammonium ions are needed for a neutral solid.
walkthrough:
**Decode the fizzing test**

Great start, fizzing when acid is added is the classic carbonate test. It tells you $\text{CO}_2$ gas is made.

Chemical rule:
$$\text{CO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decode the litmus test**

Next, hot NaOH giving a gas that turns red litmus blue is the classic ammonium test. That gas is ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$.

Chemical rule:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine to find R**

So R must contain both ammonium ions, $\text{NH}_4^+$, and carbonate ions, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$. That rules out any sulfate salt, which would not fizz with HCl.

**Balance the charges**

Remember, a solid salt must be electrically neutral. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has a +1 charge and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ has a -2 charge.

Balancing rule:
$$2 \times (+1) + (-2) = 0$$
So you need two ammonium ions for every one carbonate ion, giving $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$.

options.A: Shows the right ions but the charges do not balance. One $\text{NH}_4^+$ (+1) with one $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ (-2) gives a net -1 charge, so this formula cannot exist as a neutral solid.
options.B: Correct on both tests and on charge. It contains $\text{NH}_4^+$ so it releases $\text{NH}_3$ with hot NaOH, and it contains $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ so it releases $\text{CO}_2$ with HCl. Two +1 ions balance one -2 ion perfectly.
options.C: Incorrect formula writing. Hydrogencarbonate is $\text{HCO}_3^-$ with a -1 charge, so the correct ammonium salt would be $\text{NH}_4\text{HCO}_3$. The formula $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{HCO}_3$ has a net +1 charge and is not neutral.
options.D: Contains ammonium so it would give $\text{NH}_3$ with hot NaOH, but sulfate, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, does not react with dilute HCl to give a gas. It would fail the fizzing test.
